issue.title: Command chips: one-gesture bob runs from Obsidian notes
issue.description: Typing `run: bob …` in an inline code span, or a `bob-run` fence, gives a quiet ▶ chip. One click or ⌘↵ runs it through Bob Command Mode the way the sheet's Ctrl+Enter would. A chip holds one command or a whole `&&` sequence, and its run state shows in place. The copy-chip plugin becomes `bob-chips` and owns both kinds, and the GTD rows that hold bob commands become command chips.

payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: copyChipSerialize can emit a bob-copy fence that an indented body line closes early — it counts fence runs only at column 0, so text "a\n  ```\nb" serializes with a ``` marker and the "  ```" body line closes it (payload truncates to "a"). runChipSerialize avoids this with closerAware; copy was left byte-stable for C11. Fix by counting runs after leading whitespace, update copy vectors deliberately, and re-pin COPY_VECTORS_SHA256 in scripts/test-command-chips-grammar.cjs.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: commandChipAt only shields run chips inside math and comments that open on the same line. A run chip inside a multi-line %% / <!-- --> comment block or a $$ block that opened on an earlier line still resolves for ⌘↵ (Live Preview hides it via the syntax tree, the pure rule does not). The keymap phase (bob-cli-nu.6) or a small follow-up should track cross-line comment and math state in commandChipAt, outside fences.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: pre-existing check failures that reproduce on the clean base: (1) docs-check published URLs: docs/develop/plugins/architecture.md:74 -> /develop/validation/ (bob-plugins docs/develop/architecture.md quotes `docs/develop/validation.md`; same failure on a clean bf13f43 worktree; also noted by bob-cli-nu.2 and bob-cli-nh.7.1.3); (2) load-sensitive 25 ms perf flakes in test:unit, already tracked by bob-cli-io (frees-marks) and bob-cli-km (event-link-times); both pass alone.

Grammar phase done in bob-plugins plugins/bob-chips (0.6.0 -> 0.7.0), rebased onto the engine commit 591998e. Shared one-pass chipScanLine (kind-tagged copy|run; run spans also skip same-line math and %%/HTML comments); copyChipScanLine is now its copy filter. runChipParseContent / runChipScanLine / runChipParseFenceInfo / runChipSerialize (bob-run fence; refuses a block in a table cell; fence marker outruns indented closer-like lines); chipLinkSpans (md links and images, wikilinks and embeds, autolinks, bare http(s) URLs, outside code spans); commandChipAt implements rules 1-7 with frozen none / ambiguous{via,message} / ready{via,chip}; block chips carry fence:{open,close}; task scan generalized as chipScanTaskScope. api.commandChips v1 (version, parse, scanLine, parseFenceInfo, fencePayload, serialize, chipAt) beside the unchanged copyChips v2, plus a fallback namespace. Verified: scripts/fixtures/command-chips-vectors.json (20 chips, 22 non-chips, 4 mixed, 15 serialize, 10 fence_info, 16 link_spans, 33 chip_at covering every state and via); test-command-chips-grammar.cjs (pins the copy vectors sha256) and test-command-chips-roundtrip.cjs (5000-case property test), both in test:unit; a 200k-case differential fuzz of copy parse/scan/fenceInfo/serialize/chipAt against the pre-change bundle was byte-identical; 202/202 chip and copy-card tests; test:perf 9/9 (Live Preview at 21.6 of 35 ms); build:check, docs:inventory:check, and validate (12/12) green; docs-check lint, drift, and strict build pass. Docs: bob-chips.md "Command chip grammar" plus the ⌘↵ rule; plugin-apis.md "Command chips". Deployed with bob plugins sync -p bob-chips: synced and enabled, the vault bundle matches the build, and a smoke load of the vault bundle answers commandChips.chipAt. The only full test:unit and docs-check failures are pre-existing (see the follow-up notes).
